sections.title: Part 1: Quick Inferences
sections.passage:
Debbie pushed the button and waited for the lights to change.

Baby James spat the mashed vegetables straight back at his father.

The only noise in the room was the rustle of paper whenever Tom turned a page.

sections.title: JILL'S JOB
sections.passage: As Jill worked, she hummed softly to herself. Just one bin to go and then she would start on the vacuuming. Things were going well. At this rate she would be home before her kids were up for breakfast.

responses.prompt: At what time of the day does she do her work?

sections.title: AT THE VILLAGE
sections.passage: By the time we reached the small village the sun was going down. After so long on the road we were glad to be able to take off our boots and rub our sore feet.

responses.prompt: What time of the day was it?
How did they get to the village?

sections.title: MONARCH BUTTERFLIES
sections.passage:
Monarch butterflies lay their eggs on the underside of the swan plant. There the eggs can grow, safe from the wind and sun. When they hatch, the tiny caterpillars eat their egg shells. Then they start to eat the leaves of the plant they are on.

They eat all the time and grow quickly. As they grow, they shed their skins many times because the skin does not stretch to fit the new body. When they have finished growing, the caterpillars make cocoons and hang upside down from a leaf or the stem of the plant.

While they are inside their cocoons many changes take place. As these things happen the cocoons change colour from light to dark green.

After about three weeks the butterfly is ready to hatch. At first, the new butterfly is weak and unable to move, but it slowly gains strength and is able to fly away.

responses.prompt: Why are butterfly eggs not found on the top side of leaves?
What do the caterpillars eat first?
What would happen if they didn't shed their skins?
What colour is the cocoon to begin with?
When is the butterfly ready to fly away?
responses.response: wen the wings are fully developed

questionScores.rationale: 'idk' is not an attempted answer to where Debbie was (a pedestrian crossing).
Correctly identifies cleaning as Jill's job.
'Night' reasonably aligns with the overnight/early-morning timing implied by being home before the kids wake.
'Afternoon' reasonably aligns with the sun going down (late in the day), given benefit of doubt.
Correctly identifies walking, inferred from sore feet and boots.
Gives a different reason (hiding/camouflage) rather than the text's stated reason — safety from wind and sun.
Correctly identifies egg shells as the first food.
Does not explain the mechanism — that the skin wouldn't stretch to fit the growing body.
Incorrect — the text states the cocoon starts light green, not white.
Reasonably captures the maturation process (developing before flying), matching the text's gaining-strength idea.
